findings.title: Required end-to-end MCP request/response tests for the seven new tools are missing
findings.evidence: phase-100380 (roadmap/phase-100380-binding-closure.md) §8 'Required Tests' lists 'End-to-end tests (a full MCP request/response for each new tool)'; `grep -rn 'summarize|config_get|config_set|config_profiles|config_profile_apply|ranking_env' crates/clio-mcp/src/protocol_tests.rs crates/clio-mcp/src/http_tests.rs crates/clio-mcp/src/stdio_tests.rs` returns no matches; the new tests only call the in-process dispatcher/seam: config_tools_tests.rs:20 (`crate::write_tools::dispatch`), nfr7_tests.rs:99 (`write_tools::dispatch`), summarize_tools_tests.rs:58 (`summarize_with_extractor`). No test sends `tools/call` through `McpHandler`/stdio/HTTP for summarize, config_*, or ranking_env_*. The DoD bullet 'Required tests pass (unit, integration over MCP, contract, regression, security/masking, failure-mode; ...)' (phase file line 300) silently drops the end-to-end category.
findings.recommendation: Add a transport-level `tools/call` test per new tool (or one loop over the seven names) asserting the MCP envelope (`isError`/`structuredContent`), and either include e2e in the DoD enumeration or record a deliberate exception.
findings.resolution: Added `protocol_tests::new_tools_round_trip_over_tools_call` (crates/clio-mcp/src/protocol_tests.rs): one loop sends a real `tools/call` JSON-RPC frame through `McpHandler::handle_message` for all seven new tools and asserts the MCP envelope (`result.isError` / `result.structuredContent.ok` plus the serialized text content). The six config/ranking tools assert `isError=false`; `summarize` asserts its documented fail-closed `isError=true` + `code=not_implemented` (no extraction provider at the transport level). The DoD 'Required tests pass' bullet now enumerates 'end-to-end transport-level `tools/call`'. Real output: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib` -> 235 passed; 0 failed (test `protocol::protocol_tests::new_tools_round_trip_over_tools_call ... ok`).

findings.title: ranking_env_set/config_profile_apply have no operational effect in the running MCP process, are not persisted, and the recorded limitation misstates this as 're-resolves on restart' without naming a debt owner
findings.evidence: runtime_open.rs:120 builds the retriever/hub env from `RankingEnv::system_defaults()`; the read/write paths use that frozen `state.env` (read_retrieve.rs:58 intent gate; write_tools.rs:149 and store_write.rs:55 admission). profile_ops.rs:122-141 patches only `Runtime.ranking`; clio-config config/mod.rs:152 initializes `Runtime.ranking` to `system_defaults()`, `finish_boot` loads no ranking from overlays, and validate.rs:69-77 forbids `config_set` on `ranking.*`, so nothing persists. phase-100380 lines 333 and 405 call it 'the restart-scoped ranking snapshot ... re-resolves on restart', but a restart resets to defaults; the limitation also fails the task rule that a known limitation states 'which phase owns the debt'.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-32; §4.9.5.E; developer task 'Known limitations state (a) what is missing, (b) why, (c) which phase owns the debt'
findings.recommendation: Correct the limitation text (the patch is process-local and discarded at restart, and does not affect in-process retrieval/admission), name the owning follow-up phase, and either wire propagation into state.env/retriever or document process-lifetime semantics in the tool descriptions.
findings.resolution: Documentation path (the alternative the recommendation permits). Corrected known limitation 2 and the Final Status wording in the phase file: the patch applies only to the `clio-config` session runtime, is readable back through `ranking_env_get`/`config_get`, is discarded at process exit (a restart resets to defaults; nothing is persisted to an overlay), and does not retune the already-open retrieval/admission snapshot (`McpState.env`, the retriever's `RankingEnv`, and the hub env clone are fixed at open). The `ranking_env_get`, `ranking_env_set`, and `config_profile_apply` tool descriptions in `schema_config_defs.rs` now state those process-lifetime semantics. Owner named: the live-path wiring track (Phase 100400), with the note that the specific ranking-propagation item is not in that phase's current scope and needs an explicit scope assignment by the Remedy Approver. Live wiring was deliberately not implemented: the phase out-scopes effective-config precedence changes, and propagation would require interior mutability across `McpState.env`, the shared `Arc<HybridRetriever>` (`set_ranking_env` needs `&mut`), and the hub's env clone (crates/clio-retrieve/src/hybrid.rs:120). Recommendation adjusted: the 'wire propagation' half remains a follow-up, now recorded with an owner.

findings.title: DoD checkbox 'Required approval obtained' is marked complete while the tool_schema approval is only requested/pending
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100380-binding-closure.md:306 `- [x] Required approval obtained (tool_schema publish approval)`; the only artifact is the 'Approval requested' subsection at line 336 and Final Status line 405 '( ... the pending `tool_schema` publish approval decision)'; phase section 6/§9 say the decision is owned by the Remedy Approver step.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100380 §6 Agent Decision Boundary; §9 Definition of Done
findings.recommendation: Mark the approval DoD entry as pending (or split it into 'request recorded [x]' and 'approval obtained [ ]') so the pipeline sees the open decision.
findings.resolution: Split the DoD entry in the phase file into two: `- [x] Required approval request recorded (...)` and `- [ ] Required approval obtained (...) — **pending**; the Remedy Approver step owns the decision`. The pipeline now sees the open decision.

findings.title: The configured extractor success path is never exercised; only the fail-closed branch and the injected seam are tested
findings.evidence: summarize_tools.rs:52-67 (`configured_extractor` -> `build_extractor_from(&effective, bearer, HttpTransport::default())`) is only reached in its failure branch: T100380-03 calls `write_tools::dispatch(&s, "summarize", {"scope":"bank"})` with no provider (summarize_tools_tests.rs:126-138); all success tests inject a stub via `summarize_with_extractor` (summarize_tools_tests.rs:56-62). No test drives the real provider wiring, although phase §8's Verification Rule says 'Implementation claims must be supported by actual test output, not inspection alone'.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100380 §8 Verification Rule; AC-100380-01 evidence text
findings.recommendation: Add a test that sets `extract.url` to a local stub endpoint (or an injectable transport) and asserts the configured path produces a persisted gist; otherwise record the provider wiring as inspection-only.
findings.resolution: Refactored `configured_extractor` and added `summarize_with_transport<T: Transport + 'static>` (crates/clio-mcp/src/summarize_tools.rs) so the real factory + adapter are testable without network I/O. New test `summarize_tools_tests::configured_extractor_path_persists_gist` configures `extract.url` through the real `config_set` tool, then drives `build_extractor_from` + `TemplateApiExtractor` with a stub `clio_write::Transport` and asserts the persisted gist (`stored_gist == "stub-sidecar gist"`). Real output: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib` -> `summarize_tools::summarize_tools_tests::configured_extractor_path_persists_gist ... ok`.

findings.title: Bank-scope summarize silently drops archived items from the report, and item scope does not exclude discarded items while bank scope does
findings.evidence: summarize_tools.rs:126-128 skips `row.archived` with no `skipped[]` entry, while item scope returns NotFound for archived (summarize_tools.rs:94-99); the bank filter inherits `include_discarded=false` (inspect_query.rs:104-106), while item scope reads via `get_memory_item` (sqlite_memory.rs:38-41), which does not check `discarded_at`. The report is documented as 'items summarized, skipped, and why' (phase §5 Task 1).
findings.recommendation: Record archived/discarded items under `skipped` with reasons (or document the exclusion in the schema description) so the report is complete and both scopes behave consistently.
findings.resolution: Bank scope now sets `include_discarded=true` and pushes a `skipped` entry with reason `archived` or `discarded` for each excluded row, so the report is complete (no silent drop). Item scope now reports archived/discarded as a `skipped` report (`item_is_archived` for archived; `get_item_identity` returning `None` with the item present means discarded) instead of summarizing inactive items. The `summarize` schema description states the archived/discarded contract. Tests: `bank_scope_reports_summarized_and_skipped` (asserts reasons `no snapshot to summarize from`, `archived`, `discarded`; count summarized=1, skipped=3) and `item_scope_skips_archived_and_discarded` (both scopes skip, gist unchanged). Real output: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib` -> both `... ok`.

findings.title: config_set published schema does not state the omitted-scope default
findings.evidence: schema_config_defs.rs:44-56 declares `scope` as an optional enum with no `default` and no default text; config_tools.rs:89-93 (and clio-config dispatch) silently default an omitted scope to `session`.
findings.requirement_ref: §4.9.2 item 6 ('Optional parameters marked `?` MAY be omitted; defaults MUST be those stated here or in the published schema')
findings.recommendation: Add `"default": "session"` (or say 'defaults to session') to the config_set scope property.
findings.resolution: The published `config_set.scope` property now carries `"default": "session"` (and the description says 'default session'). New test `config_tools_tests::config_set_schema_states_session_default` reads the published pack and asserts the default. Real output: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib` -> `config_tools::config_tools_tests::config_set_schema_states_session_default ... ok`.

findings.title: New test source files do not use the AGENTS.md-mandated file header
findings.evidence: config_tools_tests.rs:1-5, summarize_tools_tests.rs:1-6, and nfr7_tests.rs:1-6 carry only Copyright/SPDX plus a one-line `//!` summary; the mandated '# Responsibility / ## Owns / ## Does not own / ## Boundary' structure is absent, while AGENTS.md says 'Every Rust source file MUST use the following header structure' and the developer task repeats 'New/modified Rust files use the exact AGENTS.md header'.
findings.recommendation: Add the mandated header to the three new files, or amend AGENTS.md to exempt test-only modules (several pre-existing *_tests.rs use the short form).
findings.resolution: Added the full AGENTS.md header (`# Responsibility` with a truthful one-line responsibility, `## Owns`, `## Does not own`, `## Boundary`) to `summarize_tools_tests.rs`, `config_tools_tests.rs`, and `nfr7_tests.rs`. Verified by inspection: `grep -n '## Owns|## Does not own|## Boundary'` finds all sections in each file.

findings.title: New code comments reference the private phase number/phase concept; the developer log claims no such leakage
findings.evidence: New files embed phase-numbered test IDs and a phase reference: summarize_tools_tests.rs:73,107,123-126 (T100380-xx), config_tools_tests.rs:35,117,142,179 (T100380-xx), nfr7_tests.rs:16 ('required by the phase'). The developer task's roadmap-isolation rule says never reference roadmap phases or phase numbers from code or comments; developer-task-r1.log line 109 states 'No roadmap/phase-number leakage in clio-mcp sources'.
findings.recommendation: Use phase-agnostic test names (or explicitly adopt the repo-wide T<phase-id> convention and fix the log claim). Pre-existing files (e.g. crates/clio-hygiene/src/audit_tests.rs:7) show the same T-ID pattern.
findings.resolution: Renamed the phase-numbered Rust test functions to phase-agnostic names (`t100380_01_summarize_item_regenerates_gist` -> `summarize_item_regenerates_gist`, `t100380_02_snapshots_are_byte_identical` -> `snapshots_are_byte_identical`, `t100380_03_fail_closed_without_generator` -> `fail_closed_without_generator`) and removed every `T100380-xx` / 'required by the phase' reference from the new test files and the phase-file AC evidence. Verified: `grep -rn '100380' crates/clio-mcp/src` now matches only the pre-existing `schema_tests::pack_publishes_no_roadmap_phase_number` guard (which asserts the published pack names no phase), and `grep -rn 'the phase'` in the new files returns nothing. The stale developer log claim is superseded by this remediation.

findings.title: summarize mutates but silently ignores dry_run=true because it is read-bound, bypassing the dry-run fail-closed guard
findings.evidence: write_tools.rs:68-71 returns read-bound names before the `dry_run_unsupported` guard; summarize is in `bound_read_tools` (lib.rs:160) and not in `DRY_RUN_TOOLS` (write_tools.rs:40-49); summarize_tools.rs:192-197 writes the gist unconditionally. §4.9.4.G lists `dry_run` as a common parameter for all core tools ('Validate and report without durable mutation when the tool mutates').
findings.recommendation: Either implement a no-write dry_run for summarize or reject dry_run=true explicitly (as other mutators do) instead of performing the durable write.
findings.resolution: Implemented the real no-write `dry_run` path (the first option in the recommendation, matching §4.9.4.G): `summarize` reads `dry_run`, `regenerate` skips `Store::update_memory_item` when it is true, and the report carries `dry_run` plus the gists it would regenerate. `dry_run` is now published in the summarize schema. New test `summarize_tools_tests::dry_run_reports_without_writing` asserts `count.summarized=1` with the would-be gist reported and the stored gist still `old prose`. Real output: `cargo test -p clio-mcp --lib` -> `summarize_tools::summarize_tools_tests::dry_run_reports_without_writing ... ok`.
